reviews.rationale: Source-bounded replay of the CY2025 Q3 packet against the stored CY2025 Q2 baseline. All figures are displayed GAAP values in USD_million rounded, compared sequentially (Q3 vs Q2), not year-over-year; no adjusted/non-GAAP or per-share measures are in either packet. Supported implication: the revenue-to-common-earnings bridge is internally coherent on the displayed rows. Total revenue net of interest expense rose 1625 (26463 -> 28088, +6.14% of baseline), and the host arithmetic mix attributes that entire increase to the two listed components (NII +563, +3.84%; noninterest income +1062, +9.01%) with an unlisted residual of 0, so no unexplained revenue remainder exists in this packet. Noninterest expense rose only 154 (+0.9%), so the revenue increase exceeded the expense increase, and the provision for credit losses fell 297 (-18.66%). Pretax income rose 1768 (7688 -> 9456, +23% of baseline) and net income rose 1353 (7116 -> 8469, +19.01%). Net income applicable to common rose 1215 (6825 -> 8040, +17.8%), a smaller relative gain than net income because preferred stock dividends rose 138 (291 -> 429, +47.42%). Material counterpoint: the tax line is the largest relative mover in the packet, +415 (+72.55% of baseline), far outpacing the +23% pretax change, so the effective tax rate on these displayed rows rose materially; that compresses the conversion of pretax to net income and means the +19.01% net income gain understates the +23% pretax gain. The preferred dividend increase (+47.42%) is a second, separate drag between net income and common earnings. Both are visible in the displayed rows but neither is explained by them. Missing evidence: the packet contains no causal drivers, no segment or line-item decomposition beyond the ten selected facts, no balance-sheet or capital items, no per-share or share-count data, no year-over-year comparatives, no adjusted measures, no rate/volume attribution, and no management commentary. The host arithmetic mix is explicitly not a causal explanation, and the boundary states that no durability, valuation, or trading conclusion is established. I therefore record no causal claims: the stored alert carries no trusted statement-line metadata, no stored driver fact is source-explicitly linked to a target metric, and I do not use an observed metric as its own cause. I also do not infer absolute loss dollars from the provision rate change, and I do not attribute the pretax or net income totals to the listed components, since the packet supplies no reconciliation of those totals. Research-state decision: needs_review. The event is complete against all ten required_event_metrics and shows no unresolved conflicts, but the two largest relative movers (tax expense and preferred dividends) are unexplained by the selected facts, and the thesis carries no assumptions, catalysts, or invalidation conditions against which to judge durability. Status and conviction are preserved and downstream decisions remain blocked pending a sourced explanation of the tax and preferred-dividend movements and a fuller filing basis. No trade, valuation, or recommendation is made.

message.content:
# BAC-2025-Q3-REVENUE-TO-COMMON-EARNINGS-BRIDGE — Research-State Replay

**Thesis** `th_286f2279e84b46d6ac22` (BAC, US, active, conviction 3) · **Alert** `fa_7c5343da1e8f44eda29a` (earnings, as_of 2025-10-15) · **Review** `tr_25747e86780c4f559b80` · thesis now **version 2**

**Basis discipline.** Every figure below is a displayed GAAP value in USD_million rounded. All comparisons are **sequential (CY2025 Q3 vs CY2025 Q2)** — the baseline is the quarter ended 2025-06-30, the event the quarter ended 2025-09-30. Neither packet contains year-over-year comparatives, adjusted/non-GAAP measures, or per-share data, so no YoY or adjusted claim is made. "Relative change" figures are percent of the Q2 baseline, not percentage points.

## Supported implication
The revenue-to-common-earnings bridge is internally coherent on the displayed rows. Total revenue net of interest expense rose 1625 (26463 → 28088, +6.14% of baseline). The host arithmetic mix assigns that entire increase to the two listed components — net interest income +563 (+3.84%) and noninterest income +1062 (+9.01%) — with an **unlisted residual of 0**, so no unexplained revenue remainder exists in this packet. Noninterest expense rose only 154 (+0.9%), materially less than the revenue increase, and the provision for credit losses fell 297 (−18.66%). Pretax income rose 1768 (7688 → 9456, +23% of baseline); net income rose 1353 (7116 → 8469, +19.01%); net income applicable to common rose 1215 (6825 → 8040, +17.8%).

## Material counterpoint
The **tax line is the largest relative mover in the packet**: +415 (+72.55% of baseline), far outpacing the +23% pretax change. On these displayed rows the effective tax rate therefore rose materially, compressing the conversion of pretax into net income — which is why the +19.01% net income gain is smaller than the +23% pretax gain. A second, separate drag sits between net income and common earnings: preferred stock dividends rose 138 (291 → 429, +47.42%), so common earnings grew +17.8% versus net income's +19.01%. Both movements are visible in the rows but **not explained by them**. I do not infer absolute loss dollars from the provision rate change, and I do not attribute the pretax or net income totals to the listed components — the packet supplies no reconciliation of those totals.

## Missing evidence
No causal drivers; no segment or line-item decomposition beyond the ten selected facts; no balance-sheet, capital, or reserve detail; no share counts or per-share metrics; no year-over-year comparatives; no adjusted measures; no rate/volume attribution; no management commentary. The host arithmetic mix is explicitly arithmetic, not causal, and the boundary states no durability, valuation, or trading conclusion is established. The thesis itself carries no assumptions, catalysts, or invalidation conditions against which to test durability.

## Research-state decision
**needs_review**, impact **mixed**. The event is complete against all ten `required_event_metrics` with no unresolved conflicts, but the two largest relative movers (tax expense, preferred dividends) are unexplained by the selected facts. I recorded **no causal claims**: the stored alert carries no trusted statement-line metadata, and no stored driver fact is source-explicitly linked to a target metric — I did not use an observed metric as its own cause.

## Verification
- Review persisted at thesis version 2; status **active** and conviction **3** preserved.
- `decision_hold: true`, `actionability: blocked`, `decision_hold_alert_id: fa_7c5343da1e8f44eda29a` — confirmed by re-read after the review.
- Alert `fa_7c5343da1e8f44eda29a` acknowledged (version 2).
- Next review set to 2026-11-07.

No trade, valuation, or recommendation was made or implied.
